subject.title: fix(google): bound realtime live-session HTTP requests

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a supported Google SDK WebSocket connection-timeout seam for Google Live, rather than merge an HTTP-only timeout that cannot bound `ai.live.connect()`?
rationale: The current SDK exposes no timeout or abort handle through the bridge's Live connection path, so choosing an SDK upgrade, upstream change, or an owned transport boundary is not a safe mechanical repair decision.

options.title: Pursue an SDK-backed Live deadline
options.body: Keep this PR open only as context and request a replacement that uses a supported connection cancellation/timeout mechanism with real stalled-WebSocket proof.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Do not add a parallel transport implementation until the Google SDK exposes a supported Live connection deadline seam.

recommendation.title: Pursue an SDK-backed Live deadline
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open only as context and request a replacement that uses a supported connection cancellation/timeout mechanism with real stalled-WebSocket proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent Google realtime timeout work provides the clearest recent history for separating the HTTP and WebSocket transport boundaries.
